message.content:
Here’s a mix of classic, modern, and cult‑favorite horror films you might enjoy:

| Year | Title | Director | Why it’s worth watching |
|------|-------|----------|------------------------|
| 1978 | **The Shining** | Stanley Kubrick | A masterclass in psychological dread and atmospheric tension. |
| 1980 | **The Thing** | John Carpenter | A tense, claustrophobic sci‑fi horror with groundbreaking practical effects. |
| 1984 | **A Nightmare on Elm Street** | Wes Craven | Introduces Freddy Krueger and blends dream logic with visceral scares. |
| 1991 | **The Silence of the Lambs** | Jonathan Demme | A chilling crime thriller featuring Hannibal Lecter. |
| 2002 | **28 Days Later** | Danny Boyle | A fast‑moving post‑apocalyptic film that redefined zombie cinema. |
| 2004 | **Saw** | James Wan | Known for its intricate puzzles and moral dilemmas. |
| 2007 | **Paranormal Activity** | Oren Peli | Low‑budget found‑footage film that creates an unsettling sense of realism. |
| 2010 | **The Conjuring** | James Wan | A supernatural thriller grounded in true‑story folklore. |
| 2012 | **The Cabin in the Woods** | Drew Goddard | A meta‑take on horror tropes that subverts expectations. |
| 2015 | **It Follows** | David Robert Mitchell | A fresh take on the “invisible stalker” concept with a haunting soundtrack. |
| 2017 | **Get Out** | Jordan Peele | A socially conscious horror that blends satire with genuine terror. |
| 2019 | **Midsommar** | Ari Aster | A daylight horror that turns the genre on its head with vivid visuals. |
| 2020 | **The Invisible Man** | Leigh Whannell | A modern retelling that uses technology as a source of fear. |
| 2021 | **A Quiet Place Part II** | John Krasinski | Builds on the original’s silence‑based tension with new threats. |
| 2023 | **Evil Dead Rise** | Lee Cronin | A fresh entry in the franchise that amps up gore and humor. |

Feel free to pick based on your preferred sub‑genre—psychological, supernatural, slasher, or something more experimental!
